Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Ethan (Redwood) / Lina, Devon, Anika (Orchid)
Links shared: //redwood.link/poc-results (results sheet), //redwood.link/burst-playbook (playbook draft)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick check-in, we ran the two stress suites against the dedicated pool last night — Ethan, can you give a quick readout?
[00:18] Ethan: Yeah sure, um so overall throughput was fine, sustained at nominal levels, but we saw p95 jump to 420ms during the 30s spike and up to 650ms in the 60s spike scenario. There's also some queueing on the GPU pods when the KV cache warms. Transcription note: sometimes the K V cache was transcribed as K V cash in our notes.
[00:39] Devon: Right, that 650ms is what concerns us. Our SLO target is 300ms p95 for interactive flows. We hit tail latency on our auth route which is high-cc small-context prompts.
[00:58] Ethan: We think two levers will help: temporary reserve buffer (bump reserved capacity by 15-25%) and a fast fallback path to a 7B quantized variant that has much lower token latency but slightly lower quality. The fallback would only trigger once a queue depth threshold is observed.
[01:19] Anika: How deterministic is the fallback? We need to avoid content divergence — can't have clinical content changed mid-session.
[01:31] Maya: Good point. Fallback is per-request, not per-session, but we can tie it to route-level rules. For clinical routes we can mark no-fallback. Also, we can do token-prefix caching to reduce cold KV penalties.
[01:48] Lina: Are we able to route by tenant? Some of our high-volume clinics are multi-tenant and they'd want dedicated throughput.
[01:57] Ethan: You can pin model variants per route or tenant in the rollout policy. We can also reserve capacity for those tenants within Dedicated — that's what reserved pools are for.
[02:12] Devon: On autoscale, our current thresholds are conservative: scale-out at 60% GPU utilization and scale-in at 25% for 5 minutes. That led to slow reaction during short bursts.
[02:27] Ethan: Yep, in the test we saw scale decision lag of about 45s because of the cooldown and evaluation window. We recommend adjusting to scale-out at 45% with a 30s evaluation window and scale-in at 20% with a 90s cooldown. That shortens reaction but avoids flapping.
[02:50] Maya: We also suggested an intermediate buffer — ephemeral burst queue that holds tokens for 20s and uses aggressive micro-batching. That reduces backend pressure.
[03:06] Anika: What's the cost delta on the reserve bump? Our finance team will want the monthly delta.
[03:14] Maya: I'll share the numbers this afternoon. Rough back-of-envelope: 20% reserve on current pool is ~+12% monthly spend but reduces overage by around 60% for your traffic profile. I'll put exact line items in the spreadsheet.
[03:34] Devon: There's also the security side — audit logs. We need more granular token-level logs in Private deployment for SOC 2.
[03:44] Ethan: Private supports audit logs and KMS/HSM with rotation. The current POC uses our hosted control plane but we can switch to Private control plane for the next dry run; just need approval and time to provision. There's also a small naming mismatch in the logs we've seen — "redwood-dedicate" sometimes shows up as "redwood-dedicated" in traces which was a transcription quirk.
[04:10] Lina: For the fallback model, can we run a blind evaluation? i.e., route 10% of tail traffic to the quantized model and compare with the full model offline.
[04:22] Ethan: Yup, we can do shadow evals for a day. We'll capture embeddings and responses and run diff metrics. Need the prompt set — could you share top 100 prompts for the last 30 days?
[04:35] Lina: Yeah, we'll extract that. Expect it by Friday.
[04:41] Maya: OK to recap next steps: Ethan runs burst scenarios and shadow eval, Maya sends pricing delta, Orchid provides traces and prompt set. Then we reconvene mid-next-week for a staged dry-run.
[04:55] Devon: Also, can we get an on-call window for the live run? Preferably a 2-hour block where Redwood support is standing by.
[05:04] Maya: Yes, we can schedule an on-call SE for the run. I'll include that in the invite.
[05:12] Anika: One small thing — can we get the runbook linked into our ops channel? Makes faster TTR.
[05:18] Maya: We'll post the playbook to the Slack channel and add runbook steps including rollback and model pinning.
[05:25] Ethan: I'll attach the performance logs and a short note about KV cache warmup in the results sheet.
[05:33] Lina: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[05:36] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with the items.
